subject: Post-demo: Novaloft pricing / model mix confirmation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Khan <rita.khan@novaloft.com>, Amit Rao <amit@novaloft.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-20 14:05 PDT
Subject: Post-demo: Novaloft pricing / model mix confirmation

Hi Rita / Amit — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put a firm quote together:

- Demo highlight: assistant flows (customer support + in-app guide) + search re-ranking + vector similarity for the knowledge base.
- We discussed rough monthly token volumes but I want to lock numbers to model the economics. Could you confirm expected tokens/month or daily active users + avg tokens/session?
- Suggested initial model mix (for our costing exercise): chat/generation: 60–70% tokens, embeddings: 20–30% of total tokens (heavy at vectorization time), rerank/reranking RPCs: 5–10% (short sequences but high QPS). If you have a different split, please share.
- Budget range / unit target: you mentioned procurement would like a target $/1M tokens — can you share the target and the monthly budget band?

I've attached a mutual action plan and a pricing primer (hosted vs. reserved) so you can see where discounts come from. Next steps I propose: you send the token estimate and any procurement constraints; we’ll return two cost scenarios (hosted pay-as-you-go + 12-month reserved capacity) and a recommended model/quantization profile to hit their unit target.

Thanks — happy to hop back on a short call if helpful.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Amit Rao <amit@novaloft.com>

Cc: Rita Khan <rita.khan@novaloft.com>, procurement@novaloft.com
Date: 2027-06-21 09:12 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Novaloft pricing / model mix confirmation

Vanessa — thanks for the follow up and the docs. Quick answers from our side: we ran a rough sizing exercise this morning.

- Usage: ~12k DAU in phase 1, avg 1.8 sessions/user/day, avg ~350 tokens per session (combined user + assistant). That puts us at ~22.6M tokens/month as a starting point. We expect growth to ~75M tokens/mo in 6–9 months if adoption goes well.
- Preferred model mix (current thinking): chat/generation (assistant): 60% of tokens, embeddings (indexing + semantic search): 30% of tokens, rerank: 10% (higher QPS but smaller token payloads).
- Budget band: target budget is $6k–$12k/month for phase 1. Procurement goal: blended unit <= $800 per 1M tokens if possible.
- Questions: 1) Do you need committed throughput to hit that unit price? 2) How do embeddings pricing compare to chat (we use embeddings heavily for search volume spikes)?

We can join a short call with procurement next week to align.

— Amit Rao
Product Lead, Search | Novaloft
amit@novaloft.com

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 09:12 AM Amit Rao <amit@novaloft.com> wrote: (internal header preserved)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Novaloft pricing / model mix confirmation

Amit — this is super helpful, thanks. High-level responses below and a quick plan to get you a model-by-model estimate by EOD tomorrow.

1) Blended unit economics: with your ~22.6M tokens/mo starting point and the proposed mix (60/30/10), a hosted (pay-as-you-go) blended estimate lands around $780–$920 per 1M tokens depending on exact model family and sequence lengths. That range assumes standard batching and no advanced reserved discounts.

2) Embeddings vs chat pricing: embeddings are charged on a per-embedding-call basis (or per-embedding-token equivalent in some pricing tiers) and because embedding vectors are dense they can dominate cost during indexing bursts. In practice, your 30% embedding proportion will push visible costs during re-index windows but amortize over retrieval calls. We will include separate lines for: embedding indexing, embedding inference at query time, chat generation, and rerank RPCs.

3) Reserved capacity: to hit a blended $500–$650 per 1M tokens we typically see customers commit to a 12-month reserved pool sized for steady-state (not peak) traffic and enable quantization + batching. So yes — a committed term materially changes the unit price.

Next steps (I’ll action):
- Sergio / Ben and I will prepare two scenarios for you by EOD tomorrow: (A) hosted estimate at your starting volume; (B) 12-month reserved projection with suggested commit to hit $500–$650 / 1M tokens. Each scenario will include per-model line items and assumptions (seq len, tokens per call, batching uplift).
- Please confirm whether the 60/30/10 split is final or if you want us to model a 70/20/10 and a 50/40/10 sensitivity.
- If procurement wants to align, propose a 30-min sync on Thurs 2027-06-24 — we can bring finance and solutions engineering.

I'll attach a one-page illustrative cost table in the next email.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

- Inputs received: starting volume ~22.6M tokens/mo, target blended <= $800 / 1M tokens, model mix 60/30/10, expectation growth to ~75M tokens/mo.
- Deliverables: 1) Hosted scenario (line-item per model), 2) Reserved 12-month scenario (commit sizes to hit $500–$650 / 1M), 3) Sensitivity table for 50/40/10 and 70/20/10, 4) Short note on which quantization options and batching settings we recommend for each model family.
- Owner: Sergio for reserved math + commit sizing; Ben for embedding indexing costs and vector storage rough; Vanessa to own client communication + procurement sync.
- Ops ask: include a note on whether prefix/KV caching could reduce active token counts for assistant flows (likely 8–12% uplift in effective throughput).

I'll draft the two-scenario spreadsheet and include an assumptions tab. Once Vanessa confirms the meeting we should loop in Alex Martinez from Solutions Engineering for implementation notes.
